newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma's Suu Kyi praises U.S. for imposing sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Burma's Suu Kyi praises U.S. for imposing sanctions.

text.p: Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi praised the United States on Friday for imposing sanctions against Rangoon's military leaders and said Washington should have a clear conscience that it made the right decision.

"When the bill was introduced in Congress it was made quite clear that sanctions would come in if there is large-scale repression of the movement for democracy in Burma," Suu Kyi told a news conference. "And I think all of you who have been following events here over the last five or six months would... know that repression has increased rather than decreased."

"I respect Clinton...it is good to know there are people in this world who are serious about what they say," Suu Kyi said in her first formal comment since the U.S. decision was made on Tuesday. Washington imposed economic sanctions on Burma as a public condemnation of human rights abuses and the military regime's repression of the democracy movement led by Suu Kyi.

Suu Kyi said was not surprised by the reaction of Burma's neighbours who said the sanctions would not impact Burma's application to become an official member of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

But she said she hoped ASEAN would come to understand the position of Burma's opposition. "We're not children. We know what to expect. We are not anti-ASEAN at all... We are in favour of joining regional organisations, but at the right time of course."

Suu Kyi told the news conference that the sanctions had come at the right time because of the growing crackdown on her opposition movement. The news conference was held at a home near her house since reporters were not allowed past barricades which block entry to Suu Kyi's street,
